# polars-online

> Streaming / online regression, clustering and regime models for Polars. A Rust core,
> reachable three ways with identical numerics: a chunk-fed `ModelBank` (hand it a
> `LazyFrame` and it chunks it), a `LazyFrame` query that streams, and the `online`
> command line over files. Memory is O(state), not O(data), so a model fits a stream
> that does not fit in RAM.

Python 3.12+, `polars>=1.34,<3`. `pip install polars-online`. `numpy` is an optional
extra, needed only by `ModelBank.gram()` and by `po.gram`, `po.corr` and `po.sim`.
No pandas.

The two Python surfaces, in full:

```python
import polars as pl
import polars_online as po

spec = po.spec.ewridge(
    "ridge",
    targets=["ret"], features=["signal_a", "signal_b"],
    clock="ts",                    # a Datetime column, so the clock parameters are durations
    half_life=pl.duration(minutes=10), gap_cap=pl.duration(minutes=5),
    group="stock_id",              # one independent state per stock
)

# As a loop: feed chunks of any size; the state is yours to save
bank = po.ModelBank([spec])
for chunk in chunks:
    out = bank.fit_predict(chunk)     # one struct column per spec, named after it
bank.save("bank.state")

# As a query: the same numbers, streamed by polars, state written when the source ends
(pl.scan_parquet("ticks/*.parquet")
   .online.fit_predict([spec], save_state="bank.state")
   .sink_parquet("fitted.parquet"))
```

**Rules that are easy to get wrong.**

- **One name differs between the two spellings**: the Python builder is
  `po.spec.ewridge(...)`, and the same model in a spec dict or a TOML file is
  `type = "ew_ridge"`. Every other model is spelled identically in both places.
- **Predictions are out-of-sample by construction.** A row's `pred` is computed from the
  state as it stands *before* the update that uses that row's target. Never fit a row
  and then score it: the `pred` the library returns is already out-of-sample.
- **Chunk invariance is a guarantee.** The same stream fed as one chunk or a thousand
  gives identical output, bit for bit, and a test enforces it. The one exception is the
  `coef` field: it is filled on each group's last row in every chunk, and every
  `coef_every` learned rows, so its schedule follows the chunking.
- **Decay runs on the clock, not on row count.** A `Datetime`, `Date` or `Duration`
  clock takes its clock parameters (`half_life`, `gap_cap`, `window_size`, ...) as
  durations: `pl.duration(minutes=10)`, a `timedelta` or `"10m"`. A numeric clock takes
  plain numbers in its own units. Either mixture is refused, naming the parameter.
  `gap_cap`, `session` / `session_gap` and `restart_after_step_back` say what happens
  across a gap, a session boundary or a clock that goes backwards. A step back is
  refused unless `restart_after_step_back` is set and the step is larger, which starts
  the model over; a smaller one is a late row, refused.
- **The clock need not be a time.** Sort by a feature, clock on it, and the half-life is
  a bandwidth in that feature's units. The fit is then a local regression in it (LOESS
  with a one-sided exponential kernel), and `ew_cov` clocked the same way gives local
  moments.
- **`weight_sum` is accumulated weight**, before this row's update and before its own decay —
  the same definition in every model. `min_weight` is in those units, so it is a
  weight, not a number of rows.
- **A zero-weight row is legal** and means "advance the clock, learn nothing", including
  as the first row of a stream.
- **Every spec adds one struct column**, named after the spec. `weight_sum` is in every one;
  the linear models add `pred_<target>`, `resid_<target>` and `coef`; diagnostics add
  theirs when switched on.
  [OUTPUTS.md](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online/blob/main/docs/OUTPUTS.md) lists
  every model's fields, and `frame.online.unnest(specs)` flattens the column into plain
  columns.

**Every surface streams.** There is no in-memory-only form: the expression namespace was
removed because polars hands a stateful user expression its whole column, so it could
not stream. The three surfaces, and how each loads and saves a state:

| surface | run it | load a state | save a state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ModelBank`, fed chunks or handed a `LazyFrame` | `bank.fit_predict(chunk)` | `po.ModelBank.load(path)` | `bank.save(path)` |
| a query | `lf.online.fit_predict(...)` | `load_state=` | `save_state=` |
| the `online` command line | `online --config bank.toml` | `--resume`, or `load_state` in the TOML | `--save-state`, or `save_state` in the TOML |

A state file is versioned msgpack, written atomically, and loads on macOS, Linux and
Windows alike.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online#readme): the guide — how a bank sees
  a stream, the three surfaces, every model with its update equations, performance
- [Introduction](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online#introduction): the four words
  the README uses (spec, model bank, stream and chunk, state) and the smallest complete
  example
- [How a bank sees a stream](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online#how-a-bank-sees-a-stream):
  clock, decay, groups, weights, warm-up, nulls, row order — the semantics every model
  shares
- [Models](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online#models): all 21, each with its
  recursion, its builder and its Rust source
- [Against scikit-learn](https://github.com/hgilde/polars-online#against-scikit-learn):
  `SGDRegressor` measured beside `sgd` and `ewridge`. It covers accuracy (the same, to
  the noise ceiling), throughput, what a prediction saw, the short-history case where
  the exact solve wins, and the wide-`k` case where sklearn wins by batching. Row by
  row, `sgd` is the faster one and agrees with it.

## API reference

- [Spec builders](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/spec.html): every model's
  builder, with every keyword and its default
- [ModelBank, fit_predict, predict](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/polars_online.html):
  the objects and functions the package exports
- [Frame namespaces](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/namespaces.html):
  `lf.online.*`, `df.online.*`
- [Evaluation](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/eval.html)
- [Gram accessors](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/gram.html)
- [Correlation toolkit](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/corr.html)
- [Stream transforms](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/stream.html)
- [Window operators](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/ops.html): `po.ewm_mean`,
  `po.rewm_mean`, `po.ewm_sum`, `po.rewm_sum`, `po.ewm_rate`, `po.rewm_rate`,
  `po.increment` -- Polars expressions over a stream's clock, run by
  `lf.online.with_windows(*exprs, **named, clock=...)` one pass, O(window) memory;
  an expression looking ahead is also a spec's target (`targets=[expr.alias(...)]`),
  resolved by the bank's own window core and learned once its window has closed
  and the `embargo` (at least its `window_size` for `fit_predict`) has passed
- [Simulation](https://hgilde.github.io/polars-online/sim.html)
